# funSmooth

Turns curves observed on a common grid `r` (e.g. summary functions such as
K, L or g estimated for several samples) into a functional data object
(`fda::fd`), using a penalised B-spline smoother.

The input is a table with one column for the grid (`r_value` by default)
and one column per curve.

```{r}
#| label: function-funSmooth

#' Smooth curves observed on a common grid into a functional data object
#'
#' Fits a penalised B-spline smoother ([fda::smooth.basis()]) to curves observed on the same grid `r`, for example summary functions (K, L, g) estimated for several samples. The table must contain one column with the grid (`r_value` by default) and one numeric column per curve.
#'
#' If `smooth.basis()` fails, a second attempt is made with a second derivative penalty (`Lfdobj = 2`) and `lambda = max(lambda, 1e-4)`, with a warning; the settings actually used are stored in the result.
#'
#' Units: `unit` is the unit of the `r` column (free text, e.g. `"pixel"` or `"micron"`). With `to_micron = TRUE` (only from `"pixel"`) the grid is multiplied by the microns per pixel `mpp`, given directly or as `mpp = mpp_ref * mag_ref / magnif`. The curve values are rescaled according to `fun_type`: L has the unit of a length (`* mpp`), K of an area (`* mpp^2`), g and `"none"` are left unchanged. `rangeval` and `breaks` are in the unit of the `r` column and are converted with it.
#'
#' @param df A `data.frame` or `data.table` with the grid column and one numeric column per curve.
#' @param norder Spline order (`norder` in fda). Must be a positive integer.
#' @param Lfdobj Order of the derivative used in the roughness penalty (`Lfdobj` of [fda::fdPar()]): a non-negative integer smaller than `norder`, or an `Lfd` object.
#' @param r_col Name of the grid column. `NULL` (default) means `"r_value"`.
#' @param centered If `TRUE`, `r` is subtracted from every curve before smoothing (L(r) - r).
#' @param nbasis Number of basis functions. If `NULL`, `min(30, max(norder + 1, floor(length(r) / 4)))`. If it is not smaller than the number of grid points it is reduced to `max(norder + 1, length(r) - 1)`. Ignored when `breaks` is given.
#' @param breaks Optional knot vector (strictly increasing, from `rangeval[1]` to `rangeval[2]`); then `nbasis = length(breaks) + norder - 2`.
#' @param lambda Smoothing penalty, a non-negative number. If `NULL`, it is chosen by generalised cross-validation (GCV), with the same basis and penalty used for the fit.
#' @param rangeval Range of the basis, `c(min, max)`. If `NULL`, `range(r)`. Must contain all the grid values.
#' @param fun_type Summary function in the curves: `"none"` (default), `"L"`, `"K"` or `"g"`. Used for the labels and to rescale the values when converting units.
#' @param unit Unit of the `r` column, a single string (default `"pixel"`).
#' @param to_micron If `TRUE`, converts from pixels to microns (requires `unit = "pixel"` and one of `mpp` or `magnif`).
#' @param mpp Microns per pixel.
#' @param magnif Magnification of the coordinates (e.g. 20 or 40), alternative to `mpp`.
#' @param mpp_ref,mag_ref Microns per pixel at a reference magnification, used with `magnif`. Default: 0.25 micron/pixel at 40x.
#' @param verbose If `TRUE`, prints messages on the choices made.
#' @param ... Other arguments passed to [fda::smooth.basis()] (e.g. `wtvec`).
#'
#' @return An object of class `spafun_fd`, a list with:
#'   - `fd`: the smoothed curves, an `fd` object (one replicate per curve, named after the curve columns);
#'   - `fdPar`: the `fdPar` object actually used for the fit;
#'   - `basis`: the B-spline basis;
#'   - `mat`: the matrix of curves (converted and centred, as smoothed);
#'   - `r`: the grid (converted);
#'   - `centered`: whether `r` was subtracted from the curves;
#'   - `fun_type`: the summary function;
#'   - `unit`: the unit of `r` in the result;
#'   - `settings`: list with the smoothing parameters actually used (`norder`, `Lfdobj` as derivative order, `nbasis`, `breaks`, `rangeval`, `lambda`, `lambda_method` `"gcv"` or `"user"`, `df` of the GCV fit, `fallback`) and the unit conversion (`unit_in`, `to_micron`, `mpp`).
#'
#'   See [print.spafun_fd()] for the methods.
#' @seealso [fda::smooth.basis()], [fda::pca.fd()]
#' @importFrom fda create.bspline.basis fdPar smooth.basis
#' @export
#' @examples
funSmooth <- function(
  df,
  norder = 6,             # spline order
  Lfdobj = 4,             # derivative order in the penalty
  r_col = NULL,           # name of the column with the r values
  centered = FALSE,       # center by r before smoothing
  nbasis = NULL,          # allow user to set number of basis functions
  breaks = NULL,          # alternative: provide a coarser breaks vector
  lambda = NULL,          # smoothing penalty; if NULL chosen by GCV
  rangeval = NULL,        # override range(r) if desired
  fun_type = c("none", "L", "K", "g"),
  unit = "pixel",         # unit of the r column
  to_micron = FALSE,      # convert pixels to microns
  mpp = NULL,             # microns per pixel
  magnif = NULL,          # or magnification of the coordinates
  mpp_ref = 0.25,         # microns per pixel at mag_ref
  mag_ref = 40,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
) {
  # 0. Input checks: they only stop early, with a clear message, on input
  #    that would make the smoothing fail or behave unexpectedly
  is_count <- function(x) {
    is.numeric(x) && length(x) == 1 && is.finite(x) && x == round(x)
  }
  is_flag <- function(x) isTRUE(x) || isFALSE(x)
  is_pos <- function(x) {
    is.numeric(x) && length(x) == 1 && is.finite(x) && x > 0
  }

  if (!is.data.frame(df)) {
    stop("`df` must be a data.frame or a data.table, not a ",
         class(df)[1], ".", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!is.null(r_col) &&
      !(is.character(r_col) && length(r_col) == 1 && !is.na(r_col))) {
    stop("`r_col` must be NULL or a single column name.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!is_count(norder) || norder < 1) {
    stop("`norder` (spline order) must be a positive integer.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (is.numeric(Lfdobj)) {
    if (!is_count(Lfdobj) || Lfdobj < 0) {
      stop("`Lfdobj` must be a non-negative integer or an Lfd object.",
           call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (Lfdobj >= norder) {
      stop("`Lfdobj` (", Lfdobj, ") must be smaller than the ",
           "spline order `norder` (", norder, ").", call. = FALSE)
    }
  } else if (!inherits(Lfdobj, "Lfd")) {
    stop("`Lfdobj` must be a non-negative integer or an Lfd object.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!is.null(nbasis) && (!is_count(nbasis) || nbasis < norder)) {
    stop("`nbasis` must be an integer not smaller than `norder` (", norder,
         ").", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!is.null(breaks)) {
    if (!is.numeric(breaks) || length(breaks) < 2 || anyNA(breaks) ||
        is.unsorted(breaks, strictly = TRUE)) {
      stop("`breaks` must be a strictly increasing numeric vector.",
           call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (!is.null(nbasis)) {
      warning("`nbasis` is ignored when `breaks` is supplied.", call. = FALSE)
    }
  }
  if (!is.null(lambda) &&
      !(is.numeric(lambda) && length(lambda) == 1 && is.finite(lambda) &&
        lambda >= 0)) {
    stop("`lambda` must be NULL or a single non-negative number.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!is.null(rangeval) &&
      !(is.numeric(rangeval) && length(rangeval) == 2 &&
        all(is.finite(rangeval)) && rangeval[1] < rangeval[2])) {
    stop("`rangeval` must be NULL or c(min, max) with min < max.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!is_flag(centered)) stop("`centered` must be TRUE or FALSE.", call. = FALSE)
  if (!is_flag(verbose)) stop("`verbose` must be TRUE or FALSE.", call. = FALSE)
  fun_type <- match.arg(fun_type)
  if (!(is.character(unit) && length(unit) == 1 && !is.na(unit) &&
        nzchar(unit))) {
    stop("`unit` must be a single non-empty string.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!is_flag(to_micron)) stop("`to_micron` must be TRUE or FALSE.", call. = FALSE)
  if (isTRUE(to_micron)) {
    if (unit != "pixel") {
      stop("`to_micron = TRUE` converts from pixels: `unit` must be ",
           "\"pixel\", not \"", unit, "\".", call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (is.null(mpp) == is.null(magnif)) {
      stop("With `to_micron = TRUE`, give either `mpp` or `magnif`.",
           call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (!is.null(mpp) && !is_pos(mpp)) {
      stop("`mpp` must be a single positive number.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (!is.null(magnif) &&
        !(is_pos(magnif) && is_pos(mpp_ref) && is_pos(mag_ref))) {
      stop("`magnif`, `mpp_ref` and `mag_ref` must be single positive ",
           "numbers.", call. = FALSE)
    }
  } else if (!is.null(mpp) || !is.null(magnif)) {
    warning("`mpp` and `magnif` are ignored when `to_micron = FALSE`.",
            call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (isTRUE(centered) && fun_type %in% c("K", "g")) {
    warning("`centered = TRUE` subtracts r, which makes sense for L ",
            "functions, not for ", fun_type, ".", call. = FALSE)
  }

  # 1. Robustly extract r
  rvals <- if (is.null(r_col)) "r_value" else r_col
  if (!rvals %in% names(df)) {
    stop("Column '", rvals, "' not found in `df`; set `r_col`.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  r <- df[[rvals]]
  if (!is.numeric(r) || any(!is.finite(r))) {
    stop("Column '", rvals, "' must be numeric, without NA or infinite ",
         "values.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (length(unique(r)) < 2) {
    stop("Column '", rvals, "' must contain at least 2 distinct values.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  # 2. Extract functional matrix (all columns other than r)
  curve_cols <- setdiff(names(df), rvals)
  if (length(curve_cols) == 0) {
    stop("`df` has no curve columns besides '", rvals, "'.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  is_num <- vapply(as.data.frame(df)[curve_cols], is.numeric, logical(1))
  if (!all(is_num)) {
    stop("Curve columns must be numeric; not numeric: ",
         paste(curve_cols[!is_num], collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE)
  }
  mat_fun <- as.matrix(as.data.frame(df)[setdiff(names(df), rvals)])
  if (is.null(colnames(mat_fun))) {
    colnames(mat_fun) <- paste0("S", seq_len(ncol(mat_fun)))
  }
  if (anyNA(mat_fun)) {
    warning("The curves contain ", sum(is.na(mat_fun)), " NA values: ",
            "smooth.basis() may fail.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  # 2b. Optional conversion from pixels to microns: r, rangeval and breaks
  #     are lengths; the values are rescaled according to fun_type
  unit_out <- unit
  mpp_used <- NULL
  if (isTRUE(to_micron)) {
    mpp_used <- if (!is.null(mpp)) mpp else mpp_ref * mag_ref / magnif
    value_power <- switch(fun_type, L = 1, K = 2, g = 0, none = 0)
    r <- r * mpp_used
    mat_fun <- mat_fun * mpp_used^value_power
    if (!is.null(rangeval)) rangeval <- rangeval * mpp_used
    if (!is.null(breaks)) breaks <- breaks * mpp_used
    unit_out <- "micron"
    if (verbose) message("Converted from pixel to micron: mpp = ", mpp_used)
  }

  # 3. Optional centering
  if (isTRUE(centered)) {
    mat_fun <- sweep(mat_fun, MARGIN = 1, STATS = r, FUN = "-")
  }

  # 4. Determine range
  if (is.null(rangeval)) rangeval <- range(r, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (min(r) < rangeval[1] || max(r) > rangeval[2]) {
    stop("`rangeval` (", rangeval[1], ", ", rangeval[2], ") must contain ",
         "all the r values (", min(r), ", ", max(r), ").", call. = FALSE)
  }

  # 5. Choose nbasis sensibly if not provided
  n_r <- length(r)
  if (!is.null(breaks)) {
    # If the user supplied breaks, follow fda convention
    nbasis_calc <- length(breaks) + norder - 2
    if (verbose) message("Using user-supplied breaks; nbasis computed as: ", nbasis_calc)
    genbasis <- create.bspline.basis(rangeval = rangeval, nbasis = nbasis_calc, norder = norder, breaks = breaks)
  } else {
    if (!is.null(nbasis)) {
      nbasis_calc <- nbasis
    } else {
      # default heuristic: up to 30 bases but not larger than roughly n_r/4
      nbasis_calc <- min(30, max(norder + 1, floor(n_r / 4)))
    }
    if (nbasis_calc >= n_r) {
      if (verbose) message("nbasis (", nbasis_calc, ") >= number of observations (", n_r, "); reducing nbasis to avoid overparameterization")
      nbasis_calc <- max(norder + 1, n_r - 1)
    }
    genbasis <- create.bspline.basis(rangeval = rangeval, nbasis = nbasis_calc, norder = norder)
  }

  # 6. Choose lambda if not provided
  if (is.null(lambda)) {
    # Lambda determined by GCV, with the same basis and penalty of the fit
    # (the `...` are for smooth.basis, not for lambdaRamsay)
    lambda_out <- lambdaRamsay(matV = mat_fun, rValues = r,
                               sBasis = genbasis, Lfd = Lfdobj)
    lambda_val <- lambda_out$lambda
    if (verbose) message("lambda chosen by GCV: ", signif(lambda_val, 3),
                         " (df = ", round(lambda_out$df, 2), ")")
  } else {
    lambda_val <- lambda
  }

  genfdPar <- fdPar(genbasis, Lfdobj, lambda = lambda_val)

  # 7. Try smoothing with fallback strategies on error
  fdPar_used <- genfdPar
  fallback <- FALSE
  genfdSmooth <- tryCatch(
    smooth.basis(argvals = r, y = mat_fun, fdParobj = genfdPar, ...),
    error = function(e) {
      warning("smooth.basis failed: ", conditionMessage(e), "; retrying ",
              "with Lfdobj = 2 and lambda = ", max(lambda_val, 1e-4),
              " (fallback).", call. = FALSE)
      # fallback: increase penalty and use Lfdobj=2
      tryCatch(
        {
          genfdPar2 <- fdPar(genbasis, Lfdobj = 2, lambda = max(lambda_val, 1e-4))
          fit2 <- smooth.basis(argvals = r, y = mat_fun, fdParobj = genfdPar2, ...)
          fdPar_used <<- genfdPar2
          fallback <<- TRUE
          fit2
        },
        error = function(e2) {
          stop("Both primary and fallback smoothing attempts failed: ", conditionMessage(e2))
        }
      )
    }
  )

  Genfun.fd <- genfdSmooth$fd

  # 8. Set names from the unit and the summary function
  value_unit <- switch(fun_type,
                       L = unit_out,
                       K = paste0(unit_out, "^2"),
                       g = NULL,
                       none = NULL)
  value_lab <- switch(fun_type, L = "L(r)", K = "K(r)", g = "g(r)",
                      none = "Value")
  if (isTRUE(centered)) value_lab <- paste(value_lab, "- r")
  if (!is.null(value_unit)) {
    value_lab <- paste0(value_lab, " (", value_unit, ")")
  }
  fdnames <- list(paste0("Distance r (", unit_out, ")"),
                  "Sample" = colnames(mat_fun),
                  value_lab)
  Genfun.fd$fdnames <- fdnames

  # 9. Basic sanity checks
  if (!is.null(Genfun.fd$coefs)) {
    n_coefs <- ncol(Genfun.fd$coefs)
    if (ncol(mat_fun) != n_coefs) {
      if (verbose) message("Warning: number of functions in mat_fun (", ncol(mat_fun), ") != number of fd coefficient columns (", n_coefs, ")")
    } else {
      if (verbose) message("Finished smoothing: nbasis=", genbasis$nbasis, ", lambda=", fdPar_used$lambda)
    }
  } else {
    if (verbose) message("Finished smoothing but fd$coefs is NULL")
  }

  Lfd_used <- fdPar_used$Lfd
  settings <- list(
    norder        = norder,
    Lfdobj        = if (inherits(Lfd_used, "Lfd")) Lfd_used$nderiv else Lfd_used,
    nbasis        = genbasis$nbasis,
    breaks        = breaks,
    rangeval      = rangeval,
    lambda        = fdPar_used$lambda,
    lambda_method = if (is.null(lambda)) "gcv" else "user",
    df            = lambda_out$df,
    fallback      = fallback,
    unit_in       = unit,
    to_micron     = to_micron,
    mpp           = mpp_used
  )

  structure(
    list(fd = Genfun.fd, fdPar = fdPar_used, basis = genbasis, mat = mat_fun,
         r = r, centered = centered, fun_type = fun_type, unit = unit_out,
         settings = settings),
    class = "spafun_fd"
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: examples-funSmooth

# three noisy curves observed on the same grid
set.seed(1)
r <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 50)
curves <- data.frame(
  r_value = r,
  A = sin(2 * pi * r) + rnorm(50, sd = 0.1),
  B = cos(2 * pi * r) + rnorm(50, sd = 0.1),
  C = r^2 + rnorm(50, sd = 0.1)
)

res <- funSmooth(curves, verbose = FALSE)
res
plot(res)

# grid column with another name, fixed number of basis functions and a
# stronger penalty
names(curves)[1] <- "dist"
res2 <- funSmooth(curves, r_col = "dist", nbasis = 10, lambda = 1e-3,
                  verbose = FALSE)

# the result can be used directly in fda, e.g. for a functional PCA
pca <- fda::pca.fd(res2$fd, nharm = 2, harmfdPar = res2$fdPar)
pca$varprop

# L functions computed on coordinates in pixels at 40x, converted to
# microns (0.25 micron/pixel at 40x) and centred: L(r) - r
r_px <- seq(0, 200, length.out = 60)
L_px <- data.frame(r_value = r_px,
                   s1 = r_px + 5 * sin(r_px / 30),
                   s2 = r_px - 3 * sin(r_px / 40))
res_um <- funSmooth(L_px, fun_type = "L", centered = TRUE,
                    to_micron = TRUE, magnif = 40, verbose = FALSE)
res_um$unit
range(res_um$r)
head(as.data.frame(res_um))
```

```{r}
#| label: tests-funSmooth

# cubic polynomials: B-splines of order 6 reproduce them and a penalty on
# the 4th derivative does not shrink them, so the fit must be exact.
# The residuals are 0 for every lambda, so GCV is flat: these tests use a
# fixed lambda; the choice by GCV is tested on noisy curves.
r <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 51)
poly_df <- data.frame(
  r_value = r,
  a = 1 + 2 * r - r^2,
  b = r^3 - r,
  c = 0.5 * r
)
poly_mat <- as.matrix(poly_df[-1])

test_that("funSmooth returns a spafun_fd object", {
  res <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, verbose = FALSE)
  expect_s3_class(res, "spafun_fd")
  expect_named(res, c("fd", "fdPar", "basis", "mat", "r", "centered",
                      "fun_type", "unit", "settings"))
  expect_s3_class(res$fd, "fd")
  expect_s3_class(res$fdPar, "fdPar")
  expect_s3_class(res$basis, "basisfd")
  expect_equal(dim(res$fd$coefs), c(res$basis$nbasis, 3))
  expect_equal(res$fd$fdnames$Sample, c("a", "b", "c"))
  expect_identical(res$r, r)
  expect_equal(unname(res$mat), unname(poly_mat))
  expect_equal(res$basis$rangeval, c(0, 1))
  expect_equal(res$fdPar$lambda, 1e-6)
  expect_false(res$centered)
  expect_equal(res$fun_type, "none")
  expect_equal(res$unit, "pixel")
})

test_that("settings keep the parameters of the smoothing", {
  res <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, verbose = FALSE)
  s <- res$settings
  expect_equal(s$norder, 6)
  expect_equal(s$Lfdobj, 4)
  expect_equal(s$nbasis, 12)
  expect_equal(s$rangeval, c(0, 1))
  expect_equal(s$lambda, 1e-6)
  expect_equal(s$lambda_method, "user")
  expect_null(s$df)
  expect_false(s$fallback)
  expect_equal(s$unit_in, "pixel")
  expect_false(s$to_micron)
  expect_null(s$mpp)
})

test_that("polynomials of degree < Lfdobj are reproduced exactly", {
  res <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, verbose = FALSE)
  fit <- fda::eval.fd(r, res$fd)
  expect_equal(unname(fit), unname(poly_mat), tolerance = 1e-6)
})

test_that("noisy curves are smoothed close to the true curves", {
  set.seed(1)
  rr <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 101)
  truth <- cbind(sin(2 * pi * rr), cos(2 * pi * rr))
  noisy <- truth + matrix(rnorm(length(truth), sd = 0.05), ncol = 2)
  res <- funSmooth(data.frame(r_value = rr, noisy), verbose = FALSE)
  fit <- fda::eval.fd(rr, res$fd)
  expect_lt(max(abs(fit - truth)), 0.15)
  expect_lt(mean((fit - truth)^2), mean((noisy - truth)^2))
})

test_that("by default lambda is chosen by GCV with the penalty of the fit", {
  set.seed(1)
  rr <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 101)
  noisy_df <- data.frame(
    r_value = rr,
    a = sin(2 * pi * rr) + rnorm(101, sd = 0.05),
    b = cos(2 * pi * rr) + rnorm(101, sd = 0.05)
  )
  res <- funSmooth(noisy_df, verbose = FALSE)
  sel <- lambdaRamsay(res$mat, res$r, res$basis, Lfd = 4)
  expect_equal(res$fdPar$lambda, sel$lambda)
  expect_equal(res$settings$lambda_method, "gcv")
  expect_equal(res$settings$df, sel$df)
  expect_message(funSmooth(noisy_df), "GCV")
  # the arguments in ... go to smooth.basis, not to lambdaRamsay
  res_w <- funSmooth(noisy_df, wtvec = rep(1, 101), verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(unname(res_w$fd$coefs), unname(res$fd$coefs))
})

test_that("funSmooth accepts other column names, orders and one curve", {
  ref <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, verbose = FALSE)

  df2 <- poly_df[, c("a", "r_value", "b", "c")]
  names(df2)[2] <- "dist"
  res2 <- funSmooth(df2, r_col = "dist", lambda = 1e-6, verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(res2$fd$fdnames$Sample, c("a", "b", "c"))
  expect_equal(unname(res2$fd$coefs), unname(ref$fd$coefs))

  one <- funSmooth(poly_df[, c("r_value", "a")], lambda = 1e-6, verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(ncol(one$fd$coefs), 1)
})

test_that("funSmooth works on a data.table", {
  skip_if_not_installed("data.table")
  ref <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, verbose = FALSE)
  res <- funSmooth(data.table::as.data.table(poly_df), lambda = 1e-6,
                   verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(unname(res$fd$coefs), unname(ref$fd$coefs))
})

test_that("the basis follows norder, nbasis and breaks", {
  # default heuristic: min(30, max(norder + 1, floor(51 / 4))) = 12
  expect_equal(funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, verbose = FALSE)$basis$nbasis, 12)
  expect_equal(
    funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, nbasis = 15, verbose = FALSE)$basis$nbasis, 15
  )

  # with breaks: nbasis = length(breaks) + norder - 2
  res_b <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25), verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(res_b$basis$nbasis, 5 + 6 - 2)
  expect_equal(res_b$basis$params, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
  expect_equal(res_b$settings$breaks, seq(0, 1, by = 0.25))

  # spline order: for B-splines nbasis - number of interior knots = norder
  res_m <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, norder = 4, Lfdobj = 2, verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(res_m$basis$nbasis - length(res_m$basis$params), 4)
  expect_equal(res_m$settings$norder, 4)
  expect_equal(res_m$settings$Lfdobj, 2)

  # nbasis not smaller than the number of points is reduced
  small <- data.frame(r_value = seq(0, 1, length.out = 10), y = 1:10)
  expect_message(
    res_s <- funSmooth(small, nbasis = 12, lambda = 1e-6),
    "reducing nbasis"
  )
  expect_equal(res_s$basis$nbasis, 9)
})

test_that("centered subtracts r from the curves and is recorded", {
  res <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, centered = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
  expect_true(res$centered)
  expect_equal(unname(res$mat), unname(poly_mat - r))
  expect_equal(unname(fda::eval.fd(r, res$fd)), unname(poly_mat - r),
               tolerance = 1e-6)
  expect_warning(
    funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, centered = TRUE, fun_type = "K",
              verbose = FALSE),
    "L functions"
  )
})

test_that("lambda and rangeval are used", {
  expect_equal(funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 0.1, verbose = FALSE)$fdPar$lambda,
               0.1)
  expect_equal(
    funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, rangeval = c(0, 2), verbose = FALSE)$basis$rangeval,
    c(0, 2)
  )
})

test_that("fdnames follow unit, fun_type and centered", {
  res <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(res$fd$fdnames[[1]], "Distance r (pixel)")
  expect_equal(res$fd$fdnames[[3]], "Value")

  res_l <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, fun_type = "L", centered = TRUE,
                     unit = "micron", verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(res_l$fd$fdnames[[1]], "Distance r (micron)")
  expect_equal(res_l$fd$fdnames[[3]], "L(r) - r (micron)")

  res_k <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, fun_type = "K", verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(res_k$fd$fdnames[[3]], "K(r) (pixel^2)")
  res_g <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, fun_type = "g", verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(res_g$fd$fdnames[[3]], "g(r)")
})

test_that("pixels are converted to microns according to fun_type", {
  res_l <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, fun_type = "L", to_micron = TRUE,
                     mpp = 0.5, verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(res_l$r, r * 0.5)
  expect_equal(unname(res_l$mat), unname(poly_mat * 0.5))
  expect_equal(res_l$basis$rangeval, c(0, 0.5))
  expect_equal(res_l$unit, "micron")
  expect_equal(res_l$settings$mpp, 0.5)
  expect_true(res_l$settings$to_micron)
  expect_equal(res_l$settings$unit_in, "pixel")

  res_k <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, fun_type = "K", to_micron = TRUE,
                     mpp = 0.5, verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(unname(res_k$mat), unname(poly_mat * 0.25))
  res_g <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, fun_type = "g", to_micron = TRUE,
                     mpp = 0.5, verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(unname(res_g$mat), unname(poly_mat))

  # magnif: mpp = mpp_ref * mag_ref / magnif = 0.25 * 40 / 20 = 0.5
  res_m <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, fun_type = "L", to_micron = TRUE,
                     magnif = 20, verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(res_m$settings$mpp, 0.5)
  expect_equal(unname(res_m$fd$coefs), unname(res_l$fd$coefs))

  # conversion before centering: L * mpp - r * mpp
  res_c <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, fun_type = "L", to_micron = TRUE,
                     mpp = 0.5, centered = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(unname(res_c$mat), unname(poly_mat * 0.5 - r * 0.5))

  # rangeval and breaks are given in pixels and converted
  res_b <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, to_micron = TRUE, mpp = 0.5,
                     rangeval = c(0, 2), breaks = seq(0, 2, by = 0.5),
                     verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(res_b$basis$rangeval, c(0, 1))
  expect_equal(res_b$basis$params, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))

  expect_message(
    funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, to_micron = TRUE, mpp = 0.5),
    "mpp = 0.5"
  )
})

test_that("unit conversion checks its arguments", {
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, to_micron = TRUE), "mpp")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, to_micron = TRUE, mpp = 0.5, magnif = 40),
               "either")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, to_micron = TRUE, mpp = -1), "mpp")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, to_micron = TRUE, magnif = 0), "magnif")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, unit = "micron", to_micron = TRUE,
                         mpp = 0.5), "pixel")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, unit = ""), "unit")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, to_micron = "yes"), "to_micron")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, fun_type = "J"), "should be one of")
  expect_warning(funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, mpp = 0.5, verbose = FALSE),
                 "ignored")
})

test_that("verbose controls the messages", {
  expect_silent(funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, verbose = FALSE))
  expect_message(funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6), "Finished smoothing")
})

test_that("a missing grid column is an error", {
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df[-1]), "not found")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, r_col = "dist", verbose = FALSE),
               "not found")
})

test_that("fallback and failure of smooth.basis", {
  # a penalty of order >= norder makes the first attempt fail: the fallback
  # with Lfdobj = 2 is used, with a warning, and recorded in the result
  expect_warning(
    res <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, Lfdobj = fda::int2Lfd(6),
                     verbose = FALSE),
    "fallback"
  )
  expect_s3_class(res$fd, "fd")
  expect_true(res$settings$fallback)
  expect_equal(res$settings$Lfdobj, 2)
  expect_equal(res$settings$lambda, 1e-4)
  expect_equal(res$fdPar$lambda, 1e-4)
  expect_equal(res$fdPar$Lfd$nderiv, 2)
  # an argument unknown to smooth.basis makes both attempts fail
  suppressWarnings(
    expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, verbose = FALSE, foo = 1),
                 "Both primary and fallback")
  )
})

test_that("funSmooth checks its input", {
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_mat), "data.frame")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, r_col = 1), "r_col")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, norder = 0), "norder")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, norder = 2.5), "norder")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, Lfdobj = 6), "smaller than")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, Lfdobj = -1), "Lfdobj")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, Lfdobj = "a"), "Lfdobj")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, nbasis = 3), "nbasis")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, breaks = c(0, 0.5, 0.2, 1)), "breaks")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = -1), "lambda")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = "a"), "lambda")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, rangeval = c(1, 0)), "rangeval")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, rangeval = c(0.2, 1)), "rangeval")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, centered = "yes"), "centered")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df, verbose = NA), "verbose")

  bad_r <- poly_df
  bad_r$r_value[3] <- NA
  expect_error(funSmooth(bad_r, verbose = FALSE), "r_value")
  expect_error(funSmooth(data.frame(r_value = rep(1, 5), y = 1:5)),
               "distinct")
  expect_error(funSmooth(poly_df["r_value"]), "no curve columns")
  expect_error(funSmooth(cbind(poly_df, d = "x"), verbose = FALSE),
               "numeric")

  expect_warning(
    funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, nbasis = 10,
              breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25), verbose = FALSE),
    "ignored"
  )
  na_y <- poly_df
  na_y$a[5] <- NA
  expect_warning(
    tryCatch(funSmooth(na_y, verbose = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL),
    "NA values"
  )
})
```

## Methods for spafun_fd

The result of `funSmooth()` has class `spafun_fd`: it keeps the smoothed
curves together with the flag `centered`, the summary function, the unit of
`r` and the settings used for the smoothing.

```{r}
#| label: function-print.spafun_fd

utils::globalVariables(c("r", "value", "sample", "group"))

#' Methods for smoothed curves
#'
#' Methods for the objects of class `spafun_fd` returned by [funSmooth()].
#'
#' - `print()` summarises curves, basis, penalty and units.
#' - `as.data.frame()` evaluates the curves on a grid and returns a long table with columns `r`, `sample` and `value`.
#' - `plot()` draws the curves with ggplot2, optionally coloured by group.
#'
#' @param x A `spafun_fd` object.
#' @param y Not used (for compatibility with the generic).
#' @param row.names,optional Not used (for compatibility with the generic).
#' @param r_eval Grid on which the curves are evaluated. If `NULL`, the grid `x$r`.
#' @param groups Optional vector with one group per curve, named after the curves (as `x$fd$fdnames$Sample`) or in the same order.
#' @param ... Not used.
#'
#' @return `print()` returns `x` invisibly; `as.data.frame()` a data.frame; `plot()` a ggplot object.
#' @rdname spafun_fd-methods
#' @importFrom fda eval.fd
#' @importFrom ggplot2 ggplot aes geom_line geom_hline labs theme_minimal
#' @importFrom utils globalVariables
#' @export
#' @examples
print.spafun_fd <- function(x, ...) {
  s <- x$settings
  n_curves <- ncol(x$fd$coefs)
  cat("<spafun_fd> ", n_curves, " curve", if (n_curves > 1) "s", "\n",
      sep = "")
  cat("  r:          [", signif(min(x$r), 4), ", ", signif(max(x$r), 4),
      "] ", x$unit, ", ", length(x$r), " points", sep = "")
  if (isTRUE(s$to_micron)) {
    cat(" (converted from pixel, mpp = ", s$mpp, ")", sep = "")
  }
  cat("\n")
  cat("  function:   ", x$fd$fdnames[[3]], "\n", sep = "")
  cat("  centered:   ", if (isTRUE(x$centered)) "yes" else "no", "\n",
      sep = "")
  cat("  basis:      B-spline, order ", s$norder, ", ", s$nbasis,
      " basis functions\n", sep = "")
  cat("  penalty:    derivative ", s$Lfdobj, ", lambda = ",
      signif(s$lambda, 3),
      if (identical(s$lambda_method, "gcv"))
        paste0(" (GCV, df = ", round(s$df, 2), ")"),
      "\n", sep = "")
  if (isTRUE(s$fallback)) {
    cat("  note:       fallback used (Lfdobj = 2, larger lambda)\n")
  }
  invisible(x)
}

#' @rdname spafun_fd-methods
#' @export
as.data.frame.spafun_fd <- function(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE,
                                    r_eval = NULL, ...) {
  if (is.null(r_eval)) r_eval <- x$r
  if (!is.numeric(r_eval) || anyNA(r_eval)) {
    stop("`r_eval` must be a numeric vector without NA.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  vals <- eval.fd(r_eval, x$fd)
  samples <- x$fd$fdnames$Sample
  if (is.null(samples)) samples <- paste0("S", seq_len(ncol(vals)))
  data.frame(
    r      = rep(r_eval, times = ncol(vals)),
    sample = rep(samples, each = length(r_eval)),
    value  = as.vector(vals),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

#' @rdname spafun_fd-methods
#' @export
plot.spafun_fd <- function(x, y = NULL, groups = NULL, r_eval = NULL, ...) {
  d <- as.data.frame(x, r_eval = r_eval)
  samples <- unique(d$sample)
  if (!is.null(groups)) {
    if (length(groups) != length(samples)) {
      stop("`groups` must have one value per curve (", length(samples),
           ").", call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (!is.null(names(groups))) {
      if (!all(samples %in% names(groups))) {
        stop("The names of `groups` must match the curve names.",
             call. = FALSE)
      }
      groups <- groups[samples]
    }
    d$group <- factor(rep(unname(groups), each = length(unique(d$r))))
    p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = r, y = value, group = sample, colour = group))
  } else {
    p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = r, y = value, group = sample))
  }
  if (isTRUE(x$centered)) {
    p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "gray50")
  }
  p +
    geom_line(alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 0.6) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = x$fd$fdnames[[1]], y = x$fd$fdnames[[3]], colour = "Group")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: examples-print.spafun_fd

set.seed(1)
r <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 50)
curves <- data.frame(r_value = r,
                     A = sin(2 * pi * r) + rnorm(50, sd = 0.1),
                     B = cos(2 * pi * r) + rnorm(50, sd = 0.1))
res <- funSmooth(curves, verbose = FALSE)
print(res)
head(as.data.frame(res, r_eval = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)))
plot(res, groups = c(A = "sin", B = "cos"))
```

```{r}
test_that("print summarises the object", {
  res <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, fun_type = "L", to_micron = TRUE,
                   mpp = 0.5, centered = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)

  expect_output(print(res), "micron")
  expect_output(print(res), "mpp = 0.5")

})

test_that("as.data.frame returns the curves in long format", {
  res <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, verbose = FALSE)
  d <- as.data.frame(res)
  expect_named(d, c("r", "sample", "value"))
  expect_equal(nrow(d), 2 * length(r))

test_that("plot returns a ggplot, with optional groups", {
  res <- funSmooth(poly_df, lambda = 1e-6, verbose = FALSE)
  p <- plot(res)
  expect_s3_class(p, "ggplot")

  p2 <- plot(res, groups = c(b = "g2", a = "g1"))
  expect_s3_class(p2, "ggplot")
  expect_equal(as.character(unique(p2$data$group[p2$data$sample == "a"])),
               "g1")
  expect_error(plot(res, groups = 1), "one value per curve")
  expect_error(plot(res, groups = c(x = 1, y = 2)), "names")
})
```

## Choice of lambda by GCV

`lambdaRamsay()` chooses the smoothing penalty by generalised
cross-validation (GCV), following Ramsay, Hooker and Graves (2009,
*Functional Data Analysis with R and MATLAB*, ch. 5). The same `lambda` is
used for all curves and the GCV criterion is summed over them.

The search is done on `log10(lambda)`, in the interval corresponding to a
range of equivalent degrees of freedom (`dfRange`): the degrees of freedom
depend only on `lambda`, the basis and the grid, not on the data, so they
give a scale-free range. GCV is evaluated on a grid and the minimum is then
refined with `optimize()`.

It works on the elements returned by `funSmooth()`:
`lambdaRamsay(res$mat, res$r, res$basis, Lfd = 2)`, and the chosen value can
be passed back as `funSmooth(df, lambda = sel$lambda)`.

```{r}
#| label: function-lambdaRamsay

#' Choose the smoothing parameter by GCV
#'
#' @param matV Matrix with the values of the curves, one curve per column.
#' @param rValues Grid on which the curves are observed (`nrow(matV)` values).
#' @param sBasis B-spline basis (`basisfd` object).
#' @param Lfd Order of the derivative in the roughness penalty: a non-negative integer smaller than the order of `sBasis`, or an `Lfd` object.
#' @param nGrid Number of values of `log10(lambda)` on which GCV is evaluated.
#' @param dfRange Range of equivalent degrees of freedom to explore, `c(low, high)` with `Lfd < low < high < sBasis$nbasis`. If `NULL`, `c(Lfd + 0.5, min(length(rValues) / 2, nbasis - 0.5))`.
#'
#' @return A list with:
#'          - `lambda`, 
#'          - `loglam` (`log10(lambda)`), 
#'          - `df` 
#'          - `gcv` (summed over the curves) of the chosen fit, 
#'          - `fd` the smoothed curves
#'          - `fdPar` the object with the chosen `lambda`, 
#'          - `basis` 
#'          - `table` a data.frame with `loglam`, `df` and `gcv` on the grid.
#' @importFrom fda int2Lfd fdPar smooth.basis
#' @importFrom stats uniroot optimize
#' @noRd
lambdaRamsay <- function(matV, rValues, sBasis, Lfd = 2,
                         nGrid = 50,
                         dfRange = NULL)
{
  # 1. Checks
  matV <- as.matrix(matV)
  if (!is.numeric(matV) || anyNA(matV)) {
    stop("`matV` must be a numeric matrix without NA.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!is.numeric(rValues) || anyNA(rValues) ||
      length(rValues) != nrow(matV)) {
    stop("`rValues` must be numeric, without NA, with one value per row ",
         "of `matV`.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!inherits(sBasis, "basisfd")) {
    stop("`sBasis` must be a basisfd object.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  nb <- sBasis$nbasis
  norder <- nb - length(sBasis$params)
  if (inherits(Lfd, "Lfd")) {
    Lfdobj <- Lfd
    Lfd <- Lfd$nderiv
  } else {
    Lfdobj <- NULL
  }
  if (!is.numeric(Lfd) || length(Lfd) != 1 || Lfd < 0 ||
      Lfd != round(Lfd) || Lfd >= norder) {
    stop("`Lfd` must be a non-negative integer (or Lfd object) smaller ",
         "than the order of the basis (", norder, ").", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!is.numeric(nGrid) || length(nGrid) != 1 || nGrid < 3) {
    stop("`nGrid` must be a number >= 3.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (is.null(dfRange)) {
    dfRange <- c(Lfd + 0.5, min(0.5 * length(rValues), nb - 0.5))
  }
  # with lambda -> Inf the fit has Lfd degrees of freedom, with lambda -> 0
  # it has nbasis: targets outside (Lfd, nbasis) cannot be reached
  if (!is.numeric(dfRange) || length(dfRange) != 2 ||
      dfRange[1] <= Lfd || dfRange[2] >= nb || dfRange[1] >= dfRange[2]) {
    stop("`dfRange` must be c(low, high) with ", Lfd, " (Lfd) < low < ",
         "high < ", nb, " (nbasis).", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (is.null(Lfdobj)) Lfdobj <- int2Lfd(Lfd)

  # 2. Range of log10(lambda) from the degrees of freedom
  #    (df decreases with lambda)
  ll_min <- find_loglam(dfRange[2], matV, sBasis, Lfdobj, rValues)
  ll_max <- find_loglam(dfRange[1], matV, sBasis, Lfdobj, rValues)

  # 3. GCV on a grid
  grid <- seq(ll_min, ll_max, length.out = nGrid)
  fits <- lapply(grid, genfdSmoother, y = matV, basis = sBasis,
                 Lfdb = Lfdobj, tt = rValues)
  tab <- data.frame(
    loglam = grid,
    df     = vapply(fits, function(sm) sm$df, numeric(1)),
    gcv    = vapply(fits, function(sm) sum(sm$gcv), numeric(1))
  )

  indgcv <- which.min(tab$gcv)
  if (indgcv %in% c(1, nGrid)) {
    warning("GCV minimum on the border of the range: consider widening ",
            "`dfRange`.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  # 4. Local refinement around the minimum
  opt <- optimize(
    function(ll) {
      sum(genfdSmoother(ll, y = matV, basis = sBasis, Lfdb = Lfdobj,
                        tt = rValues)$gcv)
    },
    interval = c(tab$loglam[max(indgcv - 1, 1)], tab$loglam[min(indgcv + 1, nGrid)])
  )
  # keep the grid point if the refinement does not improve it
  best_ll <- if (opt$objective <= tab$gcv[indgcv]) opt$minimum else tab$loglam[indgcv]
  best <- genfdSmoother(best_ll, y = matV, basis = sBasis, Lfdb = Lfdobj,
                        tt = rValues)

  list(
    lambda = 10^best_ll,
    loglam = best_ll,
    df     = best$df,
    gcv    = sum(best$gcv),
    fd     = best$fd,
    fdPar  = fdPar(sBasis, Lfdobj, 10^best_ll),
    basis  = sBasis,
    table  = tab
  )
}

#' Penalised smoothing for a given log10(lambda)
#' @noRd
genfdSmoother <- function(loglam, y, basis, Lfdb, tt) {
  smooth.basis(tt, y, fdPar(basis, Lfdb, 10^loglam))
}

#' Degrees of freedom of the smoother for a given log10(lambda)
#'
#' The degrees of freedom depend only on lambda, the basis and the grid, not
#' on the data: one curve is enough.
#' @noRd
df_of <- function(loglam, y, basis, Lfdb, tt) {
  genfdSmoother(loglam, as.matrix(y)[, 1], basis, Lfdb, tt)$df
}

#' log10(lambda) giving `target` degrees of freedom
#' @noRd
find_loglam <- function(target, y, basis, Lfdb, tt) {
  uniroot(function(ll) df_of(ll, y, basis, Lfdb, tt) - target,
          c(-12, 8), extendInt = "yes")$root
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tests-lambdaRamsay

set.seed(2)
r_g <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 101)
truth_g <- cbind(sin(2 * pi * r_g), cos(2 * pi * r_g), sin(4 * pi * r_g))
Y_g <- truth_g + matrix(rnorm(length(truth_g), sd = 0.2), ncol = 3)
basis_g <- fda::create.bspline.basis(c(0, 1), nbasis = 25, norder = 6)

test_that("lambdaRamsay chooses lambda by GCV", {
  sel <- lambdaRamsay(Y_g, r_g, basis_g, Lfd = 2, nGrid = 20)
  expect_named(sel, c("lambda", "loglam", "df", "gcv", "fd", "fdPar",
                      "basis", "table"))
  expect_true(is.finite(sel$lambda) && sel$lambda > 0)
  expect_equal(sel$lambda, 10^sel$loglam)
  expect_equal(nrow(sel$table), 20)
  # default dfRange: c(Lfd + 0.5, min(101 / 2, 25 - 0.5))
  expect_equal(range(sel$table$df), c(2.5, 24.5), tolerance = 1e-3)
  # df decrease when lambda increases
  expect_true(all(diff(sel$table$df) < 1e-8))
  expect_true(sel$df > 2.5 && sel$df < 24.5)
  expect_lte(sel$gcv, min(sel$table$gcv) + 1e-8)
  expect_equal(sel$fdPar$lambda, sel$lambda)
  expect_equal(ncol(sel$fd$coefs), 3)
  # an Lfd object gives the same result as the integer
  sel_obj <- lambdaRamsay(Y_g, r_g, basis_g, Lfd = fda::int2Lfd(2), nGrid = 20)
  expect_equal(sel_obj$lambda, sel$lambda)
})

test_that("the GCV fit is close to the true curves", {
  sel <- lambdaRamsay(Y_g, r_g, basis_g, Lfd = 2, nGrid = 20)
  mse_gcv <- mean((fda::eval.fd(r_g, sel$fd) - truth_g)^2)
  # better than the raw data and than an almost linear fit
  expect_lt(mse_gcv, mean((Y_g - truth_g)^2))
  big <- genfdSmoother(8, Y_g, basis_g, fda::int2Lfd(2), r_g)
  expect_lt(mse_gcv, mean((fda::eval.fd(r_g, big$fd) - truth_g)^2))
})

test_that("lambdaRamsay can be combined with funSmooth", {
  df_g <- data.frame(r_value = r_g, Y_g)
  res <- funSmooth(df_g, verbose = FALSE)
  sel <- lambdaRamsay(res$mat, res$r, res$basis, Lfd = 4, nGrid = 10)
  res2 <- funSmooth(df_g, lambda = sel$lambda, verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(res2$fdPar$lambda, sel$lambda)
  expect_equal(unname(res2$fd$coefs), unname(sel$fd$coefs))
})

test_that("lambdaRamsay warns when the minimum is on the border", {
  # very noisy curves: the GCV minimum is below 18 df
  expect_warning(
    lambdaRamsay(Y_g, r_g, basis_g, Lfd = 2, nGrid = 10,
                 dfRange = c(18, 24)),
    "border"
  )
})

test_that("lambdaRamsay checks its input", {
  expect_error(lambdaRamsay(Y_g, r_g, basis_g, Lfd = 2, dfRange = c(1.5, 10)),
               "dfRange")
  expect_error(lambdaRamsay(Y_g, r_g, basis_g, Lfd = 2, dfRange = c(3, 30)),
               "dfRange")
  expect_error(lambdaRamsay(Y_g, r_g, basis_g, Lfd = 6), "Lfd")
  expect_error(lambdaRamsay(Y_g, r_g[-1], basis_g), "rValues")
  expect_error(lambdaRamsay(Y_g, r_g, "basis"), "basisfd")
  Y_na <- Y_g
  Y_na[1, 1] <- NA
  expect_error(lambdaRamsay(Y_na, r_g, basis_g), "NA")
})
```
